purpose: Define constellation as the runtime grouping principle for comparable node-level evidence emitted by cynic-node watchdog cells.

principle.definition: A constellation is a named group of nodes or cells that share a runtime function and publish comparable L0 evidence without requiring a central cortex session.
principle.why: Fleet truth needs fractal grouping above individual processes but below organs, so lifecycle can reason about build, kernel, storage, mesh, forge, and cortex runtime families deterministically.
principle.kenosis_rule: A watchdog observation must report only local evidence and bounded service status; it must not infer global health or perform rich orchestration.

constellations.name: kernel
constellations.function: Kernel primary and kernel-adjacent runtime liveness.

constellations.name: forge
constellations.function: Build runner, repo lifecycle, release validation and forge surfaces.

constellations.name: mesh
constellations.function: Synapse, DNS and access mesh reachability.

constellations.name: inference
constellations.function: Dog backend and local inference capacity.

invariants: node.constellation is a functional grouping, not a host identity
node.name must still match registry node identity when the node is declared
organ-fleet may aggregate constellations, but each cynic-node watchdog only emits local evidence
watchdog mode must start without dog or process config
dog supervision may layer on top of watchdog evidence but must not be required for L0 liveness
